content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| NETO1 | Q8TDF5 (Neuropilin and tolloid-like protein 1) | 533 aa | 60,191 Da ≈ **60.2 kDa** |
| POLL | Q9UGP5 (DNA polymerase lambda) | 431 aa | 47,271 Da ≈ **47.3 kDa** |

The NETO1 protein is heavier by ~13 kDa. Both stated masses are consistent with their sequence lengths (~110–113 Da/residue), so I used them as given.

Caveat: the POLL record's sequence appears truncated — human DNA polymerase lambda is normally 575 aa (~63.4 kDa), and this entry's sequence stops abruptly at "...GSYRRGKATCGDVDVL" (the catalytic palm region), omitting the C-terminal ~144 residues including the third catalytic aspartate (Asp-490). Per instruction I answered from the sequence/mass given; note that with the full-length 575-aa protein POLL (~63.4 kDa) would actually be the heavier of the two.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length (from sequence) | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| FICD | Q9BVA6 (Protein adenylyltransferase FICD) | 458 aa | 51,778 Da ≈ **51.8 kDa** |
| PGM1 | P36871 (Phosphoglucomutase-1) | 450 aa | 49,137 Da ≈ **49.1 kDa** |

**FICD is the heavier protein** (~51.8 kDa vs ~49.1 kDa), a difference of about 2.6 kDa. Both stated molecular weights are consistent with their respective sequence lengths (~109–113 Da/residue), so I answered from the sequences as given.

Caveat: the PGM1 record's sequence looks truncated relative to the canonical human phosphoglucomutase-1 (normally 562 aa, ~61.4 kDa) — the entry's own PTM comment cites phosphorylation at Thr-467 by PAK1, a position that does not exist in the 450-residue sequence stored here. If the full-length sequence were present, PGM1 would instead be the heavier protein.

| Gene | UniProt | Length (from sequence) | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| FICD | Q9BVA6 (Protein adenylyltransferase FICD) | 458 aa | 51,778 Da ≈ **51.8 kDa** |
| PGM1 | P36871 (Phosphoglucomutase-1) | 450 aa | 49,137 Da ≈ **49.1 kDa** |

**FICD is the heavier protein** (~51.8 kDa vs ~49.1 kDa), a difference of about 2.6 kDa. Both stated molecular weights are consistent with their respective sequence lengths (~109–113 Da/residue), so I answered from the sequences as given.

Caveat: the PGM1 record's sequence looks truncated relative to the canonical human phosphoglucomutase-1 (normally 562 aa, ~61.4 kDa) — the entry's own PTM comment cites phosphorylation at Thr-467 by PAK1, a position that does not exist in the 450-residue sequence stored here. If the full-length sequence were present, PGM1 would instead be the heavier protein.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZBTB10 | Q96DT7 | 871 aa | ~94.9 kDa (94,894 Da) |
| HDAC7 | Q8WUI4 | 762 aa | ~82.7 kDa (82,703 Da) |

**ZBTB10 is the heavier protein** (~94.9 kDa vs ~82.7 kDa for HDAC7), a difference of ~12 kDa. In both entries the stated molecular weight is consistent with the stored sequence length (~108–109 Da/residue average), so the ranking holds on the sequence-derived masses.

Caveats worth flagging: the HDAC7 record's sequence looks truncated relative to the well-known full-length HDAC7 (~952 aa, ~102 kDa) — it ends abruptly mid-catalytic domain at "...GAGSGEGFNVNVAWA" with no stop-consistent C-terminus, and the entry lacks the Chain feature even though the feature count lists one. A mutagenesis note also refers to residue "A-1118", a position far beyond the stored 762-residue sequence. Per instructions I answered from the stored sequence/mass; note that with the true full-length HDAC7 (~102 kDa) the answer would flip to HDAC7.

Histone deacetylation gives a tag for epigenetic repression and plays an important role in transcriptional regulation, cell cycle progression and developmental events (By similarity). Histone deacetylases act via the formation of large multiprotein complexes (By similarity). Involved in muscle maturation by repressing transcription of myocyte enhancer factors such as MEF2A, MEF2B and MEF2C (By similarity). During muscle differentiation, it shuttles into the cytoplasm, allowing the expression of myocyte enhancer factors (By similarity). May be involved in Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) latency, possibly by repressing the viral BZLF1 gene (PubMed:12239305). Positively regulates the transcriptional repressor activity of FOXP3 (PubMed:17360565). Serves as a corepressor of RARA, causing its deacetylation and inhibition of RARE DNA element binding (PubMed:28167758). content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Yes.**

- **JARID2** (Q92833, Protein Jumonji): **1,246 aa** (sequence length matches the annotated chain 1–1246).
- **LRRC32** (Q14392, GARP): **530 aa** as stored in this record (I counted the sequence string: 530 residues).

2 × 530 = 1,060 ≤ 1,246, so JARID2 is more than twice as long (ratio ≈ 2.35×).

Caveat: the LRRC32 record looks truncated — the canonical GARP precursor is normally ~662 aa, and this entry's metadata counts Chain, Topological domain and Transmembrane features that are absent from the feature list, with the stored sequence ending mid-LRR ("...AENRLSHLP") and no transmembrane segment. Even using 662 aa, however, the answer would still be "yes" (1246 ≥ 1324 is false — note that with 662 aa the answer would flip), so this matters: with the authoritative stored sequence (530 aa) the answer is yes.

**ADRA2B (P18089)** — 450 aa, **49,954 Da ≈ 49.95 kDa**
**ICAM3 (P32942)** — sequence given is 410 aa, **44,186 Da ≈ 44.19 kDa**

ADRA2B's product (alpha‑2B adrenergic receptor) is the heavier of the two, by about 5.8 kDa.

Caveats worth noting: the ICAM3 record looks truncated. Its stored sequence is 410 residues and ends "…LYGPKIDRATCPQH", with no transmembrane/cytoplasmic segment, even though the entry is flagged as a Precursor, is annotated as a single‑pass type I membrane protein, and its `countByFeatureType` claims a Chain, a Transmembrane feature, 2 Topological domains, 5 Domains, 15 Glycosylation sites, 6 disulfides and 4 variants — none of which appear past residue ~389 in the returned feature list (only 4 domains, 14 glycosylations, 5 disulfides, 3 variants, and no Chain/TM entries are actually present). The canonical ICAM3 is ~547 aa (~57.8 kDa), which would reverse the comparison. Per the instruction to trust the sequence, I answer from the 410‑aa sequence. The stated 44,186 Da is self‑consistent with that 410‑aa sequence (~108 Da/residue), as is 49,954 Da for the 450‑aa ADRA2B.

**USP50 (Q70EL3)** vs **SERPINB6 (P35237)**

| Gene | Accession | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| USP50 | Q70EL3 | 339 aa | ~38,955 Da ≈ **39.0 kDa** |
| SERPINB6 | P35237 | 282 aa | ~32,286 Da ≈ **32.3 kDa** |

Both stated masses are consistent with their sequences (~115 Da/residue average), so USP50 is the heavier of the two records (by ~6.7 kDa).

If the full-length sequence were used, SERPINB6 would actually be the heavier protein. The answer below follows the sequence present in the record, as instructed.

**Comparison (masses computed from / consistent with the stored sequences):**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACOT7 (O00154, cytosolic acyl-CoA thioesterase) | O00154 | 380 aa | 41,796 Da ≈ **41.8 kDa** |
| CD36 (P16671, platelet glycoprotein 4) | P16671 | 354 aa | 39,646 Da ≈ **39.6 kDa** |

Based on the record data, **ACOT7 is the heavier protein** (41.8 kDa vs 39.6 kDa, a difference of ~2.2 kDa).

Caveat: the stored CD36 sequence (354 aa) is shorter than the canonical human CD36 (472 aa, ~53 kDa). Its own annotations contradict the stored sequence — e.g. ubiquitination sites at Lys‑469 and Lys‑472, a second transmembrane helix and additional topological domains counted in the feature summary but absent from a 354‑residue chain, and no "Chain" feature spanning the sequence is listed. The stated mass (39,646 Da) is internally consistent with the truncated sequence, so by the "sequence is authoritative" rule ACOT7 wins; with the true full-length CD36, CD36 would be heavier.

"19471024"}], "value": "Multifunctional glycoprotein that acts as a receptor for a broad range of ligands. Ligands can be of proteinaceous nature like thrombospondin, fibronectin, collagen or amyloid-beta as well as of lipidic nature such as oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL), anionic phospholipids, long- and very long-chain fatty acids and bacterial diacylated lipopeptides. They are generally multivalent and can therefore engage multiple receptors simultaneously, the resulting formation of CD36 clusters initiates signal transduction and internalization of receptor-ligand complexes. The dependency on coreceptor signaling is strongly ligand specific. Cellular responses to these ligands are involved in angiogenesis, inflammatory response, fatty acid metabolism, taste and dietary fat processing in the intestine (Probable). Binds long- and very long-chain fatty acids and facilitates their transport into cells, thus participating in muscle lipid utilization, adipose energy storage, and gut fat absorption (By similarity) (PubMed:18353783, PubMed:21395585, PubMed:21610069). Mechanistically, palmitoylated CD36 captures fatty acids on the cell surface, the binding of fatty acids activates downstream kinase LYN, which phosphorylates the palmitoyltransferase ZDHHC5 and inactivates it, resulting in the subsequent depalmitoylation of CD36, a step needed to initiate the endocytic process and delivery of fatty acids into the cell (PubMed:32958780). In the small intestine, plays a role in proximal absorption of dietary fatty acid and cholesterol for optimal chylomicron formation, possibly through the activation of MAPK1/3 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway (By similarity) (PubMed:18753675). Involved in oral fat perception and preferences (PubMed:22240721, PubMed:25822988). Detection into the tongue of long-chain fatty acids leads to a rapid and sustained rise in flux and protein content of pancreatobiliary secretions (By similarity). In taste receptor cells, mediates the induction of an increase in intracellular calcium levels by long-chain fatty acids, leading to the activation of the gustatory neurons in the nucleus of the solitary tract (By similarity). Important factor in both ventromedial hypothalamus neuronal sensing of long-chain fatty acid and the regulation of energy and glucose homeostasis (By similarity). Receptor for thrombospondins, THBS1 and THBS2, mediating their antiangiogenic effects (By similarity). Involved in inducing apoptosis in podocytes in response to elevated free fatty acids, acting together with THBS1 (By similarity). As a coreceptor for TLR4:TLR6 heterodimer, promotes inflammation in monocytes/macrophages. Upon ligand binding, such as oxLDL or amyloid-beta 42, interacts with the heterodimer TLR4:TLR6, the complex is internalized and triggers inflammatory response, leading to NF-kappa-B-dependent production of CXCL1, CXCL2 and CCL9 cytokines, via MYD88 signaling pathway, and CCL5 cytokine, via TICAM1 signaling pathway, as well as IL1B secretion, through the priming and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome (By similarity) (PubMed:20037584). Selective and nonredundant sensor of microbial diacylated lipopeptide that signal via TLR2:TLR6 heterodimer, this cluster triggers signaling from the cell surface, leading to the NF-kappa-B-dependent production of TNF, via MYD88 signaling pathway and subsequently is targeted to the Golgi in a lipid-raft dependent pathway (By similarity) (PubMed:16880211)"}], "commentType": "FUNCTION"}, {"texts": Caveat: the stored CD36 sequence (354 aa) is shorter than the canonical human CD36 (472 aa, ~53 kDa). content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison (full-length canonical sequences in the database):**

| Gene | Accession | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| TNFRSF10B (TRAIL-R2 / DR5) | O14763 | 440 aa | 47,878 Da ≈ **47.9 kDa** |
| KLF11 (TIEG-2) | O14901 | 410 aa | 43,547 Da ≈ **43.5 kDa** |

**TNFRSF10B is the heavier protein** (≈47.9 kDa vs ≈43.5 kDa), a difference of ~4.3 kDa.

Caveats worth noting:
- The KLF11 record looks truncated: the canonical human KLF11 is ~510 aa with three C2H2 zinc fingers, but the stored sequence is 410 aa and stops in the middle of the first zinc-finger motif ("…VCSFPGCRKTYFKSSH"). Consistently, `countByFeatureType` claims 3 "Zinc finger" and 1 "Chain" feature, yet none appear in the feature list, and the sequence block lacks the usual crc64/md5. I answered from the sequence/mass as given.
- TNFRSF10B is a precursor with an annotated 55-residue signal peptide; the mature chain (56–440) would be only ~42 kDa, i.e. slightly *lighter* than KLF11. The comparison above uses the full translated sequences, as is standard.

**Comparison (full-length canonical sequences in the database):**

| Gene | Accession | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| TNFRSF10B (TRAIL-R2 / DR5) | O14763 | 440 aa | 47,878 Da ≈ **47.9 kDa** |
| KLF11 (TIEG-2) | O14901 | 410 aa | 43,547 Da ≈ **43.5 kDa** |

**TNFRSF10B is the heavier protein** (≈47.9 kDa vs ≈43.5 kDa), a difference of ~4.3 kDa.

Caveats worth noting:
- The KLF11 record looks truncated: the canonical human KLF11 is ~510 aa with three C2H2 zinc fingers, but the stored sequence is 410 aa and stops in the middle of the first zinc-finger motif ("…VCSFPGCRKTYFKSSH"). Consistently, `countByFeatureType` claims 3 "Zinc finger" and 1 "Chain" feature, yet none appear in the feature list, and the sequence block lacks the usual crc64/md5. I answered from the sequence/mass as given.
- TNFRSF10B is a precursor with an annotated 55-residue signal peptide; the mature chain (56–440) would be only ~42 kDa, i.e. slightly *lighter* than KLF11. The comparison above uses the full translated sequences, as is standard.

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by VTI1A or CDC42EP2? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| VTI1A | Q96AJ9 (VTI1A_HUMAN) | 163 aa | 18,995 Da ≈ **19.0 kDa** |
| CDC42EP2 | O14613 (BORG1_HUMAN) | 210 aa | 22,484 Da ≈ **22.5 kDa** |

**CDC42EP2** (Cdc42 effector protein 2) is the heavier protein, ~22.5 kDa versus ~19.0 kDa for VTI1A — a difference of ~3.5 kDa. (Even accounting for the annotated N-terminal Met removal plus N-acetylserine on CDC42EP2, its mature mass is ~22.4 kDa, still clearly heavier.)

Note on the VTI1A entry: the displayed sequence is isoform 2 at only 163 aa, which is shorter than the commonly cited ~217 aa VTI1A product, and it contains no C-terminal hydrophobic tail even though the entry's keywords and feature counts assert a transmembrane helix, two topological domains and a chain feature that are not present in the returned feature list. The 18,995 Da value is consistent with the 163-aa sequence given, so I used it as authoritative.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| VTI1A | Q96AJ9 (VTI1A_HUMAN) | 163 aa | 18,995 Da ≈ **19.0 kDa** |
| CDC42EP2 | O14613 (BORG1_HUMAN) | 210 aa | 22,484 Da ≈ **22.5 kDa** |

**CDC42EP2** (Cdc42 effector protein 2) is the heavier protein, ~22.5 kDa versus ~19.0 kDa for VTI1A — a difference of ~3.5 kDa. (Even accounting for the annotated N-terminal Met removal plus N-acetylserine on CDC42EP2, its mature mass is ~22.4 kDa, still clearly heavier.)

Note on the VTI1A entry: the displayed sequence is isoform 2 at only 163 aa, which is shorter than the commonly cited ~217 aa VTI1A product, and it contains no C-terminal hydrophobic tail even though the entry's keywords and feature counts assert a transmembrane helix, two topological domains and a chain feature that are not present in the returned feature list. The 18,995 Da value is consistent with the 163-aa sequence given, so I used it as authoritative.

| **DPH1** | Q9BZG8 (2‑(3‑amino‑3‑carboxypropyl)histidine synthase subunit 1) | 438 aa | **48.1 kDa** (48,134 Da) |
| PAK2 | Q13177 (Serine/threonine-protein kinase PAK 2) | 393 aa | **43.3 kDa** (43,274 Da) |

**DPH1 is heavier** (≈48.1 kDa vs ≈43.3 kDa), a difference of ~4.9 kDa.

Caveat: the PAK2 record's stored sequence is only 393 residues and ends abruptly mid‑kinase domain ("...KLTDFGFCAQI"), whereas canonical human PAK2 is 524 aa (~58 kDa). The listed 43,274 Da is consistent with the stored 393‑aa sequence, and per instructions the sequence is authoritative — but with the full‑length PAK2 sequence the ranking would reverse. The entry's own annotations (caspase cleavage at 212/213 yielding a ~34 kDa C‑terminal fragment "PAK‑2p34") are incompatible with a 393‑residue chain, confirming the stored sequence is truncated.

protein kinase that plays a role in a variety of different signaling pathways including cytoskeleton regulation, cell motility, cell cycle progression, apoptosis or proliferation (PubMed:12853446, PubMed:16617111, PubMed:19273597, PubMed:19923322, PubMed:33693784, PubMed:7744004, PubMed:9171063). Acts as a downstream effector of the small GTPases CDC42 and RAC1 (PubMed:7744004). Activation by the binding of active CDC42 and RAC1 results in a conformational change and a subsequent autophosphorylation on several serine and/or threonine residues (PubMed:7744004). Full-length PAK2 stimulates cell survival and cell growth (PubMed:7744004). Phosphorylates MAPK4 and MAPK6 and activates the downstream target MAPKAPK5, a regulator of F-actin polymerization and cell migration (PubMed:21317288). Phosphorylates JUN and plays an important role in EGF-induced cell proliferation (PubMed:21177766). Phosphorylates many other substrates including histone H4 to promote assembly of H3.3 and H4 into nucleosomes, BAD, ribosomal protein S6, or MBP (PubMed:21724829). Phosphorylates CASP7, thereby preventing its activity (PubMed:21555521, PubMed:27889207). Additionally, associates with ARHGEF7 and GIT1 to perform kinase-independent functions such as spindle orientation control during mitosis (PubMed:19273597, PubMed:19923322). On the other hand, apoptotic stimuli such as DNA damage lead to caspase-mediated cleavage of PAK2, generating PAK-2p34, an active p34 fragment that translocates to the nucleus and promotes cellular apoptosis involving the JNK signaling pathway (PubMed:12853446, PubMed:16617111, PubMed:9171063). content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**UNC5D is heavier.**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| UNC5D (Netrin receptor UNC5D) | Q6UXZ4 | 953 aa | **105.9 kDa** (105,880 Da) |
| NLRP7 (NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 7) | Q8WX94 | 784 aa | **90.0 kDa** (89,968 Da) |

UNC5D exceeds NLRP7 by ~15.9 kDa. (Note: the UNC5D figure is for the full precursor; the mature chain after removal of the 1–32 signal peptide would be ~102 kDa, still heavier than NLRP7.) Both stated molecular weights are consistent with their sequence lengths (~111 and ~115 Da per residue, respectively).

Minor data oddities: the NLRP7 entry's feature counts list 9 "Repeat" features and 1 "Chain" feature, but only 3 LRR repeats and no chain feature are actually present in the record; NLRP7 also lacks a molWeight-accompanying CRC64/MD5 that the UNC5D entry has. Neither affects the mass comparison.

**UNC5D is heavier.**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| UNC5D (Netrin receptor UNC5D) | Q6UXZ4 | 953 aa | **105.9 kDa** (105,880 Da) |
| NLRP7 (NACHT, LRR and PYD domains-containing protein 7) | Q8WX94 | 784 aa | **90.0 kDa** (89,968 Da) |

UNC5D exceeds NLRP7 by ~15.9 kDa. (Note: the UNC5D figure is for the full precursor; the mature chain after removal of the 1–32 signal peptide would be ~102 kDa, still heavier than NLRP7.) Both stated molecular weights are consistent with their sequence lengths (~111 and ~115 Da per residue, respectively).

Minor data oddities: the NLRP7 entry's feature counts list 9 "Repeat" features and 1 "Chain" feature, but only 3 LRR repeats and no chain feature are actually present in the record; NLRP7 also lacks a molWeight-accompanying CRC64/MD5 that the UNC5D entry has. Neither affects the mass comparison.

**MPP3 (Q13368):** 585 aa (verified by counting the sequence; ends …SWVR, consistent with the 1–585 chain and the Arg585 variant).
**NEGR1 (Q7Z3B1):** 266 aa by actual sequence count (the entry's stated length of 266 matches the sequence given).

Binds to specific sequence motif 5'-TAATTA-3' in regulatory elements of target genes (PubMed:22194193, PubMed:31691806). Also plays a key role in intestinal enteroendocrine cell differentiation by promoting differentiation of intestinal enteroendocrine cell types L, -N, -D, -I and -G (PubMed:37883554). "35982156"}], "value": "Substrate-recognition component of the Cul7-RING(FBXW8) ubiquitin ligase complex, which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins (PubMed:17205132, PubMed:18498745, PubMed:21572988, PubMed:24362026, PubMed:35982156). The Cul7-RING(FBXW8) complex mediates ubiquitination and consequent degradation of GORASP1, acting as a component of the ubiquitin ligase pathway that regulates Golgi morphogenesis and dendrite patterning in brain (PubMed:21572988). Mediates ubiquitination and degradation of IRS1 in a mTOR-dependent manner: the Cul7-RING(FBXW8) complex recognizes and binds IRS1 previously phosphorylated by S6 kinase (RPS6KB1 or RPS6KB2) (PubMed:18498745). The Cul7-RING(FBXW8) complex also mediates ubiquitination of MAP4K1/HPK1: recognizes and binds autophosphorylated MAP4K1/HPK1, leading to its degradation, thereby affecting cell proliferation and differentiation (PubMed:24362026). trace.task_prompt: Is ACOT7 at least twice as long as PTRH2? Answer yes or no with both lengths. Put exactly "yes" or "no" in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**No.**

- **ACOT7** (O00154, isoform 1 displayed): 285 aa (verified by counting the sequence).
- **PTRH2** (Q9Y3E5): 179 aa (verified by counting the sequence).

Twice PTRH2 would be 358 aa, which exceeds ACOT7's 285 aa; the ratio is ~1.59×.

**COMMD4 (Q9H0A8)** — 199 aa, 21,764 Da ≈ **21.8 kDa**
**FKBP14 (Q9NWM8)** — sequence given is 158 aa, 17,937 Da ≈ **17.9 kDa**

Based on the sequences as stored, COMMD4's product is the heavier of the two (~21.8 kDa vs ~17.9 kDa).

Caveats: the FKBP14 record looks internally inconsistent — the canonical human FKBP14 precursor is 211 aa (~24 kDa, consistent with its alternative name "22 kDa FK506-binding protein"), and the stored 158-aa sequence lacks the C-terminal EF-hand region and ER-retention signal. The entry's own feature counts (3 domains, 10 binding sites, a motif, a glycosylation site) exceed what is present in the listed 158-residue sequence, and no Chain feature coordinates are shown. If the full-length 211-aa sequence were used, FKBP14 would instead be the heavier protein. I answered from the sequence/mass actually present, as instructed.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| SKA1 | Q96BD8 (SKA complex subunit 1) | 255 aa | 29,484 Da ≈ **29.5 kDa** |
| ASB7 | Q9H672 (Ankyrin repeat and SOCS box protein 7) | 238 aa | 26,812 Da ≈ **26.8 kDa** |

I verified both residue counts by hand against the stored sequences (255 and 238), and both stated molecular weights are consistent with those sequence lengths (~115 Da/residue). So **SKA1 is the heavier protein**, by about 2.7 kDa.

Caveats worth noting: the ASB7 record's stored sequence (238 aa, ending "...RMLYNYGA") contains only the ankyrin repeats and no SOCS box, even though the entry has DOMAIN comments about a SOCS box mediating Elongin BC binding and its feature-count summary lists a Domain, a Chain and 8 repeats that are absent from the feature list (only 6 ANK repeats shown). It also annotates phosphosites and mutagenesis up to residue 216, which do fit within 238. The canonical human ASB7 is normally ~318 aa (~35 kDa), which would reverse the comparison — but per instruction I answered from the sequence/mass as given. Additionally, the two "PxVxL" motifs (63–67 = VRVFL; 73–77 = PTVKD) don't match the stated consensus in the given sequence.

The ECS(ASB7) complex acts as a negative regulator of H3K9me3 histone mark by mediating ubiquitination and degradation of SUV39H1: ASB7 is recruited to heterochromatin by CBX5 (HP1 alpha), where it associates with SUV39H1, promoting the ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation of SUV39H1 (PubMed:40440427). During mitosis, ASB7 is phosphorylated and inactivated, allowing SUV39H1 activity (PubMed:40440427). The ECS(ASB7) complex also plays a role in spindle dynamics and genome integrity by targeting the mitotic progression protein PSRC1 for proteasomal degradation in a cell cycle-dependent manner (PubMed:27697924). **Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| SKA1 | Q96BD8 (SKA complex subunit 1) | 255 aa | 29,484 Da ≈ **29.5 kDa** |
| ASB7 | Q9H672 (Ankyrin repeat and SOCS box protein 7) | 238 aa | 26,812 Da ≈ **26.8 kDa** |

I verified both residue counts by hand against the stored sequences (255 and 238), and both stated molecular weights are consistent with those sequence lengths (~115 Da/residue). So **SKA1 is the heavier protein**, by about 2.7 kDa.

Caveats worth noting: the ASB7 record's stored sequence (238 aa, ending "...RMLYNYGA") contains only the ankyrin repeats and no SOCS box, even though the entry has DOMAIN comments about a SOCS box mediating Elongin BC binding and its feature-count summary lists a Domain, a Chain and 8 repeats that are absent from the feature list (only 6 ANK repeats shown). It also annotates phosphosites and mutagenesis up to residue 216, which do fit within 238. The canonical human ASB7 is normally ~318 aa (~35 kDa), which would reverse the comparison — but per instruction I answered from the sequence/mass as given. Additionally, the two "PxVxL" motifs (63–67 = VRVFL; 73–77 = PTVKD) don't match the stated consensus in the given sequence.

The MAD2L1 product (mitotic spindle assembly checkpoint protein MAD2A) is heavier, ~23.5 kDa vs ~18.8 kDa for the sodium channel regulatory subunit beta-4 — a difference of ~4.7 kDa. Both stated molWeight values are consistent with their respective sequences (~110 Da/residue), so I used them as given.

In the open conformation they allow Na(+) ions to selectively pass through the pore, along their electrochemical gradient. The influx of Na+ ions provokes membrane depolarization, initiating the propagation of electrical signals throughout cells and tissues. If the full-length 228-aa precursor were used, SCN4B would likely be the heavier of the two, so this conclusion depends on the stored (authoritative) sequence.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**TASL (Q9HAI6)** — 301 aa, molecular weight 33,894 Da ≈ **33.9 kDa**
**ADA (P00813)** — sequence in this record is 272 aa, 30,366 Da ≈ **30.4 kDa**

Based on the sequences as stored (which are authoritative here), TASL is the heavier protein, by ~3.5 kDa.

Caveat: the ADA record's sequence looks truncated — the canonical human adenosine deaminase is 363 residues (~40.8 kDa), ending "...SPLPRVRELYDHLKDRD", whereas this entry stops at residue 272 ("...CPWSSYLTGAW"). The stored molWeight (30,366) is internally consistent with the truncated sequence, and the annotated features (secondary structure, variants, binding sites) also stop at ≤272, but a full-length ADA would be heavier than TASL. The ADA entry also lacks a Chain feature despite reporting one in its feature counts.

**Comparison**

| Gene | Accession | Length | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| OR10J5 | Q8NHC4 (Olfactory receptor 10J5) | 309 aa | 34,401 Da ≈ **34.4 kDa** |
| UPB1 | Q9UBR1 (Beta-ureidopropionase) | 288 aa | 32,424 Da ≈ **32.4 kDa** |

As stored, **OR10J5 (≈34.4 kDa)** is heavier than UPB1 (≈32.4 kDa), by about 2 kDa. Both stated molecular weights are internally consistent with their sequence lengths (~111–113 Da/residue).

Caveat: the UPB1 record's sequence looks truncated — human beta-ureidopropionase is normally 384 aa (~44 kDa), and the entry's own feature counts list a Chain, a Domain, a Modified residue and 10 natural variants that are not all present in the displayed feature list. If the full-length 384-aa protein were used, UPB1 would be the heavier one. Answering from the sequence/mass actually given, OR10J5 wins.

**Comparison**

| Gene | UniProt | Length | Mass (from sequence record) |
|---|---|---|---|
| FANCL | Q9NW38 (E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase FANCL) | 281 aa | **32.2 kDa** (32,154 Da) |
| MAS1 | P04201 (Proto-oncogene Mas) | 325 aa | **37.5 kDa** (37,465 Da) |

Based on the stored sequences, **MAS1 (37.5 kDa) is heavier than FANCL (32.2 kDa)**.

Caveats worth noting: the FANCL record's sequence looks truncated — it is 281 aa ending "...NIHLWDPENSVL", yet the entry is annotated with a RING-type zinc finger plus 8 zinc-binding sites that lie outside this range (no residue numbers >281 appear in the shown features), and the entry carries the alias "Fanconi anemia-associated polypeptide of 43 kDa (FAAP43)". The canonical FANCL protein is 375 aa (~43 kDa); with the full-length sequence FANCL would instead be the heavier protein. I answered from the sequence as instructed.

Based on the stored sequences, **MAS1 (37.5 kDa) is heavier than FANCL (32.2 kDa)**.

Caveats worth noting: the FANCL record's sequence looks truncated — it is 281 aa ending "...NIHLWDPENSVL", yet the entry is annotated with a RING-type zinc finger plus 8 zinc-binding sites that lie outside this range (no residue numbers >281 appear in the shown features), and the entry carries the alias "Fanconi anemia-associated polypeptide of 43 kDa (FAAP43)". The canonical FANCL protein is 375 aa (~43 kDa); with the full-length sequence FANCL would instead be the heavier protein. I answered from the sequence as instructed.

trace.task_prompt: Which is heavier, the protein encoded by GJA3 or ARFIP2? Give the gene symbol and both masses in kDa. Put only the gene symbol of the heavier protein in the JSON "answer" field.

content.text: I'll look up both proteins.

**Comparison**

| Gene | Accession | Length | Mass from entry sequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| GJA3 (connexin‑46) | Q9Y6H8 | 326 aa | ~36.6 kDa (36,586 Da) |
| ARFIP2 (arfaptin‑2) | P53365 | 341 aa | ~37.9 kDa (37,856 Da) |

ARFIP2's product is the heavier one, by ~1.3 kDa (and even more so if GJA3's annotated initiator‑Met removal is taken into account, ~36.5 kDa).

Caveats: the GJA3 record looks suspect — connexin‑46 is normally a 435‑residue, ~47 kDa protein (the "Cx46"/46 kDa name reflects this), yet the stored sequence is only 326 aa; the entry also lists a "Chain" feature in its counts but no chain feature is present. I answered from the stored sequence/mass as instructed.

"ECO:0000269", "source": "PubMed", "id": "31827282"}], "value": "Catalytic subunit of histone acetyltransferase HBO1 complexes, which specifically mediate acetylation of histone H3 at 'Lys-14' (H3K14ac), thereby regulating various processes, such as gene transcription, protein ubiquitination, immune regulation, stem cell pluripotent and self-renewal maintenance and embryonic development (PubMed:16387653, PubMed:21753189, PubMed:24065767, PubMed:26620551, PubMed:31767635, PubMed:31827282). Some complexes also catalyze acetylation of histone H4 at 'Lys-5', 'Lys-8' and 'Lys-12' (H4K5ac, H4K8ac and H4K12ac, respectively), regulating DNA replication initiation, regulating DNA replication initiation (PubMed:10438470, PubMed:19187766, PubMed:20129055, PubMed:24065767). Specificity of the HBO1 complexes is determined by the scaffold subunit: complexes containing BRPF scaffold (BRPF1, BRD1/BRPF2 or BRPF3) direct KAT7/HBO1 specificity towards H3K14ac, while complexes containing JADE (JADE1, JADE2 and JADE3) scaffold direct KAT7/HBO1 specificity towards histone H4 (PubMed:19187766, PubMed:20129055, PubMed:24065767, PubMed:26620551). H3K14ac promotes transcriptional elongation by facilitating the processivity of RNA polymerase II (PubMed:31827282). Acts as a key regulator of hematopoiesis by forming a complex with BRD1/BRPF2, directing KAT7/HBO1 specificity towards H3K14ac and promoting erythroid differentiation (PubMed:21753189). H3K14ac is also required for T-cell development (By similarity). KAT7/HBO1-mediated acetylation facilitates two consecutive steps, licensing and activation, in DNA replication initiation: H3K14ac facilitates the activation of replication origins, and histone H4 acetylation (H4K5ac, H4K8ac and H4K12ac) facilitates chromatin loading of MCM complexes, promoting DNA replication licensing (PubMed:10438470, PubMed:11278932, PubMed:18832067, PubMed:19187766, PubMed:20129055, PubMed:21856198, PubMed:24065767, PubMed:26620551). Acts as a positive regulator of centromeric CENPA assembly: recruited to centromeres and mediates histone acetylation, thereby preventing centromere inactivation mediated by SUV39H1, possibly by increasing histone turnover/exchange (PubMed:27270040). Involved in nucleotide excision repair: phosphorylation by ATR in response to ultraviolet irradiation promotes its localization to DNA damage sites, where it mediates histone acetylation to facilitate recruitment of XPC at the damaged DNA sites (PubMed:28719581). Acts as an inhibitor of NF-kappa-B independently of its histone acetyltransferase activity (PubMed:16997280)"}], "commentType": "FUNCTION"}, {"texts": [{"evidences": [{"evidenceCode": "ECO:0000269", "source": "PubMed", "id": "31827282"}], "value": "Plays a central role in the maintenance of leukemia stem cells in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) (PubMed:31827282). a cell-surface receptor for PDGFA, PDGFB and PDGFC and plays an essential role in the regulation of embryonic development, cell proliferation, survival and chemotaxis. Depending on the context, promotes or inhibits cell proliferation and cell migration. Plays an important role in the differentiation of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells. Required for normal skeleton development and cephalic closure during embryonic development. Required for normal development of the mucosa lining the gastrointestinal tract, and for recruitment of mesenchymal cells and normal development of intestinal villi. Plays a role in cell migration and chemotaxis in wound healing. Plays a role in platelet activation, secretion of agonists from platelet granules, and in thrombin-induced platelet aggregation. Binding of its cognate ligands - homodimeric PDGFA, homodimeric PDGFB, heterodimers formed by PDGFA and PDGFB or homodimeric PDGFC -leads to the activation of several signaling cascades; the response depends on the nature of the bound ligand and is modulated by the formation of heterodimers between PDGFRA and PDGFRB. Phosphorylates PIK3R1, PLCG1, and PTPN11. Activation of PLCG1 leads to the production of the cellular signaling molecules diacylglycerol and inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate, mobilization of cytosolic Ca(2+) and the activation of protein kinase C. Phosphorylates PIK3R1, the regulatory subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase, and thereby mediates activation of the AKT1 signaling pathway. Mediates activation of HRAS and of the MAP kinases MAPK1/ERK2 and/or MAPK3/ERK1. Promotes activation of STAT family members STAT1, STAT3 and STAT5A and/or STAT5B. central role in centriole duplication. Able to trigger procentriole formation on the surface of the parental centriole cylinder, leading to the recruitment of centriole biogenesis proteins such as SASS6, CPAP, CCP110, CEP135 and gamma-tubulin. When overexpressed, it is able to induce centrosome amplification through the simultaneous generation of multiple procentrioles adjoining each parental centriole during S phase. Phosphorylates 'Ser-151' of FBXW5 during the G1/S transition, leading to inhibit FBXW5 ability to ubiquitinate SASS6. Its central role in centriole replication suggests a possible role in tumorigenesis, centrosome aberrations being frequently observed in tumors. Also involved in deuterosome-mediated centriole amplification in multiciliated that can generate more than 100 centrioles. Also involved in trophoblast differentiation by phosphorylating HAND1, leading to disrupt the interaction between HAND1 and MDFIC and activate HAND1. Phosphorylates CDC25C and CHEK2. Required for the recruitment of STIL to the centriole and for STIL-mediated centriole amplification (PubMed:22020124). Phosphorylates CEP131 at 'Ser-78' and PCM1 at 'Ser-372' which is essential for proper organization and integrity of centriolar satellites (PubMed:30804208)"}], "commentType": "FUNCTION"}, **Comparison**

| Gene | Accession | Length (stored sequence) | Mass |
|---|---|---|---|
| PDGFRA | P16234 | 817 aa | 91,790 Da ≈ **91.8 kDa** |
| PLK4 | O00444 | 970 aa | 108,972 Da ≈ **109.0 kDa** |

Based on the sequences actually present in the records, **PLK4 is heavier** (≈109.0 kDa vs ≈91.8 kDa).

Important caveat: the PDGFRA record's sequence looks truncated. Canonical PDGFRA is 1089 aa (~122.7 kDa), and this entry's own annotations refer to residues beyond the stored length (e.g. autophosphorylation at Tyr-988 and Tyr-1018, a "Chain" feature counted in the feature summary but absent, and the C-terminus ends mid-kinase-domain at "...LASKNCVHR" with no stop-codon-consistent tail). The stored molWeight (91,790) is self-consistent with the 817-residue sequence (~112 Da/residue), so I answered from the sequence as instructed — but with the full-length PDGFRA protein, PDGFRA would be the heavier of the two.
